stem: A project maintains child modules in the same repository under the `./modules/vpc` directory. How should the calling root module declare the `source` argument, and why?
options: It should use a relative path like `./modules/vpc` so Terraform considers the module part of the same package and avoids downloading it separately.
It should use an absolute system path like `/opt/modules/vpc` so Terraform does not require running `terraform init`.
It should use a remote Git URL with `?ref=HEAD` so Terraform automatically stores independent clones in `.terraform/modules`.
It should omit the `source` argument entirely and specify only the module name because child folders in the same directory are detected automatically.
objective: Declare module blocks referencing local relative file paths and external Git or Registry sources

stem: You need to reference an external module hosted in a private Git repository, pin it to a release tag named `v2.4.0`, and ensure Git performs a shallow clone with a depth of 1. How should the `module` block be configured?
options: Set `source = "git::https://example.com/repo.git#v2.4.0"` and add a `depth` argument inside the module block.
Set `source` to the Git URL, and declare `version = "v2.4.0"` with `shallow = true` inside the module block.
Set `source` to the Git URL and execute `git clone --depth 1` manually before running `terraform plan`.
Set `source` to the Git URL with query parameters `?ref=v2.4.0&depth=1` appended to the address.
objective: Declare module blocks referencing local relative file paths and external Git or Registry sources

stem: Your root module calls a public registry module with `version = "~> 1.0"`. You update the configuration to `version = "~> 2.0"` and add a new Git-backed child module. What must you do before running `terraform plan`, and what does it accomplish?
options: Run `terraform init`, which downloads the child module files and updated versions into the local workspace directory.
Run `terraform apply -upgrade`, because modules are only updated during the apply phase of the workflow.
Run `terraform fmt`, which checks out module dependencies while verifying configuration syntax.
Run `terraform plan` directly with `-refresh=true`, which loads remote module code into memory without touching disk.
objective: Initialize module dependencies using terraform init and terraform get
